translation.english_title: Calmly, at ease, think a little and see

english_lines: “Is your vote for the Rising Sun? Our vote is for the Rising Sun itself,
Look at how the country is going and cast your vote, amma.”
notes: The opening campaign quotation remains explicitly campaign speech; `கதிரவன்` is rendered as `Rising Sun` in this quoted electoral context without importing any additional campaign text.

english_lines: Calmly, at ease, think a little and see,
Think and see about the generation that comes next,
Look at the rise and fall and place the weights,
Put barriers before the trickster and the madman,
(Calmly, at ease).
notes: `ஆற, அமர` is kept as a paired calm/settled instruction rather than compressed to a single neutral adverb.
The weighing image in `ஏற, இறங்க ... எடைகளைப் போடு` remains visible.
Verified `எத்தனுக்கும்` is translated conservatively through the source's trickster sense; the Tamil witness is not normalized.

english_lines: Who is the one who comes to you for your vote?
A worker — or one who cheats the town?
Who is the one standing in the election field?
Those who made sacrifice; those who committed fraud,
Do not trust the wretches who give money for votes, appa,
Do not push away the good one who gives his life for the country, appa,
We must hate the bribe-demons,
The one who ends the poor man's suffering must win... for that,
(Calmly, at ease).
notes: The worker / town-cheater contrast, vote-buying accusation and `லஞ்சப் பேய்கள்` as `bribe-demons` remain direct political language.
The source's compact `தியாகம் செஞ்ச வரை மோசம் செஞ்சவரு` is not silently rewritten into a grammatically repaired Tamil sentence; the English keeps its two opposed actions visible.
`உலுத்தர்கள்` is rendered as `wretches`, retaining the contemptuous colloquial register; `ப்பா` remains audible as `appa`.

source_tamil_lines: இந்த படை போதுமா, இன்னும் கொஞ்சம் வேணுமா
உறவுக்கு கரம் கொடுப்பான் எங்க வீட்டு தம்பியப்பா
உதயக் கதிருதான் உதிக்குது பாரு உடன் பிறப்பே நீ ஒன்றாக சேரு
english_lines: Ask what price — cast your vote, amma,
Look at the price of rice and cast your vote, amma,
Is this force enough, or do you want a little more?
Who is the cruel one with no principle at all?
Who is the warrior who will not bow to cruelty?
Who is the man who lives practising corruption?
Who is the noble one who tells the town about it?
For kinship he will give his hand — our house's thambi, appa,
For rights he will give his voice — the Thenpandi lion, appa,
See, the rising ray itself is rising — O udanpirappe, come together as one,
(Calmly, at ease).
notes: The rice-price and vote-price rhetoric remains literal rather than being generalized into election reform language.
`உறவுக்கு கரம் / உரிமைக்கு குரல்` is retained as hand-for-kinship / voice-for-rights, preserving Kalaignar's paired rhetorical construction.

`தம்பி`, `தென்பாண்டி சிங்கம்`, and especially `உடன் பிறப்பே` remain culturally and politically audible as `thambi`, `Thenpandi lion`, and `udanpirappe` rather than being flattened into generic supporter language.

translator_notes: The song is campaign rhetoric built from colloquial address, weighing metaphors, anti-corruption accusation, rice-price politics and kinship/rights word-pairing. The English preserves that political register instead of neutralizing it.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
